messages:
Priya Nair: FYI CI is intermittently failing in eval-runner on judge ties. root assertion: `assert consensus_score >= 0.5` but we see cases at ~0.498 and non-deterministic tie paths.
Ethan Cole: saw same in last nightly. two judges flip orders on identical prompts, tiebreaker falls through to an undefined branch.
Maya Liu: could be FP rounding from quantized models or candidate ordering nondeterminism. did we seed the shuffles everywhere?
Priya Nair: repro steps: `pytest tests/eval_runner/test_judge_tiebreak.py::test_tie_path --seed=2026 -k tie` 0% of runs fail on my laptop.
Samir Patel: infra-bot: CI matrix failing on linux-py3.10-gpu-quantized x3. job=build-3245. artifacts: /artifacts/3245/judge-fail.log
Ethan Cole: quick patch idea: make tiebreak deterministic: stable sort by (score desc, model_id asc), and add a float tolerance when comparing scores `if abs(a-b) < 1e-3: treat as tie`. Also return explicit fallback priority list.
Maya Liu: I prefer a combined approach: clamp floats with a configurable epsilon, *and* ensure deterministic sampling with RNG seed plumbed through the runner. Also log the quantization mode (q8/q4) per judge in failures.
Priya Nair: we should also make CI surface per-judge outputs in failure artifacts (scores, conf intervals, model variants). that'll speed debugging.
Samir Patel: I'll add extra artifact dumps and rerun matrix. For now I'll bump tolerance to 1e-2 in CI to reduce flakes while we land a proper fix.
Ethan Cole: I'll open a small PR: stable-sort + deterministic fallback ordering + small epsilon. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/eval-runner/pull/1298 (WIP).
Maya Liu: I'll add a new test that repeats the same seed 20x and fails if outputs differ; plus ensure quantized vs fp32 reporting in logs.
Priya Nair: action items: Ethan = PR for deterministic tiebreak; Maya = flaky-seed test + artifact logging; Samir = CI artifact changes + rerun matrix. I'll add these to eval-harness backlog and tag priority P1 for the week.
infra-bot: Noted. rerunning jobs after PR merge will notify thread.
Ethan Cole: one more thought 0: for ensemble judges we might compute an "ensemble confidence" by averaging calibrated logits then thresholding; that reduces reliance on pairwise ordering and makes ties rarer. can prototype after this patch.
Maya Liu: agreed, but prototype separately. main goal now: eliminate nondeterminism and improve CI visibility.
Priya Nair: +1. keeping this thread as the single source for the fix. will update when PR merges. :thumbsup:
